conclusion_text:
TURTLE TRADING -- SYSTEM 2 (DONCHIAN CHANNEL BREAKOUT): RESEARCH COMPLETE, REJECTED FOR PAPER TRADING.

Faithfully implemented (long-only, disclosed scope reduction from the original long/short futures system) and validated through the full pipeline: walk-forward, out-of-sample holdout, Statistical Auditor, Performance Analyst narrative, and a dedicated robustness analysis.

Base run (full 457-symbol frozen universe, 2016-2026, EXP-002): PASS. CAGR 28.87%, Sharpe 0.73, Max Drawdown 31.0%, 244 trades, out-of-sample expectancy +Rs.647.78/trade. Outperformed both live production strategies (MA Crossover, Mean Reversion) and Buy & Hold on CAGR.

Robustness analysis (EXP-003 through EXP-006) found the edge is NOT time-robust: tested in isolation, the second half of the window (2021-2026, the period most relevant to future deployment) produced a REJECT verdict, with out-of-sample expectancy of -Rs.113.67/trade. The full-period PASS is substantially carried by the earlier 2016-2021 era. Universe-subset and walk-forward-window-count sensitivity checks both held up fine -- only the time-period test failed.

CONCLUSION: the original Turtle methodology demonstrated genuine historical strength but insufficient temporal robustness for this research program acceptance criteria. Not eligible for paper trading. No parameter tuning or optimization was attempted or will be attempted on this result.

STANDING METHODOLOGICAL OUTCOME (applies to every future strategy in the roadmap, not just Turtle): a long backtest's aggregate PASS can hide a strategy that has already stopped working in recent years -- a dedicated recent-period-only run is now a mandatory acceptance-criteria check (see swing_research/acceptance_criteria.py), not an optional add-on. Also caught and fixed during this cycle: a capital-allocation asymmetry that made an early benchmark comparison unfair (fixed via a shared-capital-pool engine using production real risk parameters), and a symbol-format sector-mapping bug (Trade.symbol vs bare-symbol sector map).

MINERVINI TREND TEMPLATE FILTER: RESEARCH COMPLETE, VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE (not approved for paper trading, not permanently rejected).

Base run (full 457-symbol frozen universe, 2016-2026, EXP-008): PASS. 574 walk-forward trades, out-of-sample expectancy +INR244.27/trade, continuous CAGR 24.7%, Sharpe 1.038, MaxDD 32.85%. Outperformed both live production strategies on CAGR and Sharpe.

Official recent-period-only check (EXP-009, most recent 3 years): REJECT. Minervinis heavy 252-day lookback left only 2 feasible walk-forward windows in the 3-year slice (a real windowing-granularity bug in acceptance_criteria.py was found and fixed here, generically, via a new Strategy.min_lookback_days attribute -- applies to every future strategy, not just this one). After the fix, the check genuinely traded (117 trades) but REJECTed because its single non-holdout consistency window (2024-08 to 2025-02) had negative expectancy (-INR141.90/trade) -- a REJECT resting on the sign of just one window.

Independent robustness sub-period check (EXP-011, second half of the 10-year window, 2021-2026, 3 windows -- materially overlapping the same recent years): PASS, strongly. 164 trades, 100% of windows positive, OOS expectancy +INR646.28/trade, continuous CAGR 34.51%, Sharpe 1.308, MaxDD only 11.51% -- better than the 2016-2021 first half.

Unlike Turtle (where the second-half robustness result CORROBORATED the recent-period REJECT), here the two independent, methodologically valid recent-period-style checks DISAGREE. Per explicit direction, the framework does not let either result silently override the other, and does not force a PASS or REJECT to resolve the conflict. A new third standing verdict, INCONCLUSIVE, was added to swing_research/acceptance_criteria.py (determine_acceptance_verdict()) specifically for this situation: base run PASS, recent-period REJECT, with disclosed conflicting robustness evidence. Minervini is the first strategy to receive this verdict.

CONCLUSION: Minervini Trend Template Filter is INCONCLUSIVE -- neither approved for paper trading nor permanently rejected. Future evidence (additional market history as it accumulates, alternate universes, further robustness studies) may resolve the conflict either way. No parameter tuning or rule changes were made in pursuit of a different verdict at any point in this cycle -- only the acceptance-criteria frameworks windowing bug and its missing third verdict were fixed, both generically and both verified against the full test suite (443 tests) before being applied to this strategys result.

STANDING METHODOLOGICAL OUTCOME (applies to every future strategy in the roadmap): a strategys own lookback requirement can silently starve a fixed-length recent-period check of walk-forward windows -- now handled generically via Strategy.min_lookback_days. And a recent-period check and an independent robustness study CAN legitimately disagree -- the acceptance framework now has a principled third outcome (INCONCLUSIVE) for exactly that case, instead of forcing an artificial PASS/REJECT choice.

52-WEEK HIGH MOMENTUM: RESEARCH COMPLETE, VERDICT PASS.

Source: George and Hwang (2004), The Journal of Finance -- nearness to the 52-week high, cross-sectionally ranked, predicts future returns better than standard past-return momentum. Implemented as a long-only, single-vintage, top-decile (nearness percentile >=90) entry with a 126-trading-day time-stop exit and an 8% synthetic protective stop -- disclosed deviations from the source: (1) long-only, (2) single-vintage holding instead of the papers K-month overlapping-portfolio construction (the largest structural deviation, MODERATE-to-MATERIAL, directionally unknown impact), (3) deliberately NO percentile-based early exit (an earlier plan draft included one; removed before implementation per explicit direction, to avoid hybridizing the baseline test with an invented rule), (4) a protective stop-loss and position sizing convention entirely absent from the source paper (a factor-return study with zero position-level risk management), required to run this through the position-based engine at all.

Base run (EXP-013, full 457-symbol universe, 2016-2026): PASS. 311 walk-forward trades, 100% window consistency, out-of-sample expectancy +INR1576.18/trade. Continuous CAGR 22.8%, Sharpe 1.058, MaxDD 30.8%. Evidence quality HIGH (90.0/100) -- the highest of any strategy in this program so far.

Recent-period-only check (EXP-014, most recent 3 years, window count auto-reduced from 3 to 2 by the frozen strategy-aware windowing logic): PASS. 74 trades, 100% of windows positive (unlike Minervinis single-window coin-flip REJECT, this rests on 2 genuinely agreeing windows), out-of-sample expectancy +INR140.87/trade. Evidence quality MODERATE (62.6/100).

No conflicting robustness evidence -- unlike Minervini, there was no disagreement between the official recent-period check and any independent study to resolve, so determine_acceptance_verdict(PASS, PASS) returns a clean PASS with no INCONCLUSIVE involved. No robustness sub-period pass was run, per the approved plans own conditional (reserved for close/ambiguous or REJECT results).

CONCLUSION: 52-Week High Momentum is the FIRST strategy in this program to pass both the base run and the mandatory recent-period check cleanly. This is a research conclusion about statistical/methodological robustness only, not a trading recommendation -- whether and when to proceed toward paper trading remains a separate decision for the user. No parameter tuning or rule changes were made in pursuit of this or any other verdict. Zero framework changes were made during this strategys evaluation, per the 2026-08-04 platform freeze -- acceptance_criteria.py, evidence_quality.py, and cross_strategy_review.py were all used exactly as built.

THIS IS THE THIRD COMPLETED STRATEGY (after Turtle REJECTED, Minervini INCONCLUSIVE) -- the first cross-strategy research review is now due per swing_research.cross_strategy_review.is_review_due().

CROSS-SECTIONAL MOMENTUM: RESEARCH COMPLETE, OFFICIAL VERDICT PASS -- but a supplementary post-COVID robustness run REJECTs, and paper-trading registration is paused pending an explicit diversification decision (per new governance requirements approved 2026-08-04).

Source: Jegadeesh and Titman (1993), The Journal of Finance -- the foundational cross-sectional momentum paper. Implemented as long-only, single-vintage, top-decile (J=6-month formation-return percentile >=90) entry with a 126-trading-day time-stop exit and an 8% synthetic protective stop -- disclosed deviations mirror 52-Week High Momentums own approved precedent (single-vintage instead of overlapping portfolios, no percentile-based early exit, synthetic risk management absent from the source paper).

Base run (EXP-016, full 457-symbol universe, 2016-2026): PASS. 338 walk-forward trades, 100% window consistency, OOS expectancy +INR2008.58/trade. Evidence quality HIGH (90.0/100).

Recent-period check (EXP-017, most recent 3 years): PASS. 110 trades, 100% window consistency (lighter 126-day lookback never triggered the strategy-aware windowing reduction Minervini needed). OOS expectancy +INR736.26/trade. Evidence quality HIGH (78.8/100). determine_acceptance_verdict(PASS, PASS) = PASS, official, no conflict, no INCONCLUSIVE needed.

Supplementary post-COVID robustness run (EXP-018, 2020-01-01 onward, additional evidence only per explicit direction, does NOT alter the official verdict): REJECT. Out-of-sample expectancy -INR54.02/trade on 224 trades, evidence quality HIGH (90.0/100) -- a genuine, evidence-quality-strong finding that the edge did not hold specifically over the post-COVID regime.

Direct comparison against 52-Week High Momentum (the only other paper-trading strategy): Cross-Sectional Momentum is weaker on every headline metric (CAGR 20.67% vs 22.8%, Sharpe 1.046 vs 1.058, MaxDD 32.79% vs 30.8%, profit factor 1.704 vs 2.301, win rate 28.7% vs 36.0%, expectancy INR1593.98 vs INR2220.41/trade, at the base-run horizon; weaker again at the recent-period horizon). However, sector breakdown reveals genuine behavioral divergence, not a duplicate signal: 52-Week High Momentums largest winning sector (Financial Services, +INR252,890) is roughly flat for Cross-Sectional Momentum (-INR390), and Realty is 52-Week High Momentums 4th-largest winner (+INR60,408) but Cross-Sectional Momentums single worst sector (-INR28,051). Full comparison table and written diversification assessment recorded in swing_research/strategy_library/cross_sectional_momentum.md.

CONCLUSION: Research Verdict is PASS, unaffected by the post-COVID supplementary finding per explicit governance direction (Research Verdict and Deployment Status remain independent). Per the new governance step approved 2026-08-04, a clean PASS does not automatically trigger paper-trading registration -- the diversification comparison is presented to the user for an explicit decision given the mixed picture (real sector diversification, but weaker on every raw metric and a real post-COVID REJECT that 52-Week High Momentum does not share). No parameter tuning or rule changes were made in pursuit of any particular verdict. Zero framework changes were made during this strategys evaluation -- acceptance_criteria.py, evidence_quality.py, cross_strategy_review.py, and every file under deployment/ were used exactly as built. 52-Week High Momentums own paper trading continued completely uninterrupted throughout this evaluation.

THIS IS THE FOURTH COMPLETED STRATEGY. No cross-strategy review is due yet (next due after the 6th strategy, per the standing 3-strategy cadence).
